default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-079.title: VWAP first-touch hold
E-079.hypothesis: After price has traded entirely on one side of the session VWAP for a while, VWAP-benchmarked buyers (sellers) who missed the move rest orders at the day's average cost; the first bar that touches VWAP and closes back on the old side shows them absorbing the pullback sellers, so the move resumes away from VWAP (the hold, not the cross of E-001).

E-080.title: VWMA-SMA volume confirmation cross
E-080.hypothesis: Dormeier's VPC: when the volume-weighted mean of recent closes rises clearly above the plain mean, the heavy-volume bars are the higher-priced ones, i.e. size is paying up rather than drifting; with price above the mean, the side committing volume is the side of the trend, so follow the cross (mirror).

E-081.title: Heikin-Ashi colour flip after a run
E-081.hypothesis: Heikin-Ashi candles are a default chart type for many retail WIN traders, who hold while the candles stay one colour and reverse on the first opposite-colour candle; after a run of red HA candles the first green one triggers their covering and new longs together, and the shorts' stops sit just above, so follow it.

E-082.title: Agulhada do Didi
E-082.hypothesis: Didi Aguiar's 'needle' (3, 8 and 20-bar averages all crossed by one candle, then fanning out in order) is one of the most watched Brazilian retail setups; it marks the end of a compression, and the many users buy when the next candle breaks the needle candle's high in the order 3>8>20, so follow the fan-out (mirror).

E-083.title: Narrow-range streak release
E-083.hypothesis: Several consecutive bars with a range well below normal for their minute mean liquidity providers are quoting a balanced book with no initiative flow; the first bar of at least normal range that closes strongly in one direction is the first initiative order to clear that book, and the quotes pulled by the burst let it travel, so follow the release bar.

E-084.title: Larry Williams setup 9.2 trigger
E-084.hypothesis: Setup 9.2 (rising 9 EMA, a bar closing below the previous low, buy on the break of that bar's high) is taught to most Brazilian WIN day traders; their buy-stops cluster one tick above the pullback bar, so the trigger break fills them together while the pullback sellers' stops are at the same place; follow it (mirror).

E-085.title: Untested prior-session level magnet
E-085.hypothesis: Stops and breakout orders accumulate just beyond yesterday's high, low, close, open and midpoint while they stay untouched today; when price comes within a typical 15-minute move of such a level, short-term traders run it toward that liquidity before it is touched, so follow the approach toward the level.

E-087.title: Session path-efficiency trend follow
E-087.hypothesis: The share of today's total price path that is net progress from the open measures how one-sided the day is; when it rises well above its usual value for the minute, the counter side is not rotating price back, which means a persistent informed or rebalancing flow, so follow the direction when efficiency jumps.

E-088.title: Setup 123 local-bottom trigger
E-088.hypothesis: The '123' (middle of three candles makes the lowest low, here also the lowest of the window, entry on the break of the third candle's high) is a Stormer-popularised Brazilian setup; the clustered buy-stops of its users fill together at the trigger, and the sellers of the local low are trapped with stops above, so follow the trigger (mirror for tops).
